record.title: Any paid plan price satisfies the payment amount check — pay the cheapest tier price, receive the most expensive plan for 30 days
record.description: CreatePaymentQuery validates an MP payment's transaction_amount against `accepted_amounts`, which is the UNION of every non-trial plan price plus pending_charge — not the amount corresponding to the entitlement actually being granted. A payment whose amount equals ANY plan's price is accepted and ApplyPendingPlanQuery then applies whatever pending_plan_suscription (or the already-rewritten plan_suscription of a pending_payment subscription) is set, granting the most expensive plan while collecting the cheapest plan's price. The broad acceptance was added deliberately to avoid orphaned MP charges when a preference/debit was issued before a plan change (services.py:107-112 comments), but it decouples amount from entitlement in both directions. Verified deterministic exploit: (a) pending_payment subscription — create checkout preference at cheap plan, PATCH plan_suscription to expensive (PENDING_PAYMENT branch rewrites plan_suscription directly), pay the stale cheap preference -> expensive plan ACTIVE 30d; (b) active subscription — create checkout preference at current cheap plan price, then request upgrade to expensive plan (pending_plan + prorated pending_charge via RequestPlanChangeQuery), pay the stale cheap preference -> paid_amount != pending_charge so prorated=False -> pending expensive plan applied AND end_date renewed +30d. Repeatable monthly via the stale-preference cycle or a failed best-effort UpdatePreapprovalPlanQuery realignment (RequestPlanChangeQuery swallows MP errors). IssueInvoiceQuery then emits a fiscally inconsistent invoice: plan_name snapshot = expensive plan, total = cheap payment.amount.
record.root_cause: AdminApp/domains/payments/services/services.py CreatePaymentQuery lines 115-124: `accepted_amounts` unions {pending_plan-or-current price, current plan price, ALL SuscriptionPlan prices where is_trial=False, pending_charge} and only checks set membership — the granted entitlement (pending_plan or pending_payment plan_suscription) is never bound to the amount paid. `expected_amount` (line 106) is computed but used only in the error message. ApplyPendingPlanQuery (lines 281-313) applies pending_plan whenever a payment is APPROVED with renew=True; the only amount-sensitive gate is `paid_amount == pending_charge` deciding prorated-vs-full-renewal, never amount-vs-plan-price.
record.intended_behavior: A payment should only credit the entitlement its amount pays for: pending_charge for prorated upgrades, or the price of the specific plan being applied (pending_plan if set else plan_suscription for pending_payment). Stale-amount MP charges should either map amount->plan (grant the plan that amount corresponds to) or be rejected/flagged for reconciliation — as the sibling StoreApp storepayments webhook does (exact order.total match required, mismatch -> manual review) — rather than silently upgrading entitlement.

trace.description: POST /api/payments/checkout/ -> _resolve_suscription -> CreateCheckoutPreferenceQuery(suscription): preference unit_price = pending_charge or (pending_plan or plan_suscription).price snapshot at creation time; external_reference = str(suscription.id). An earlier preference keeps its creation-time amount and stays payable.
Lines 382-391 freeze unit_price + external_reference into the MP Checkout Pro preference — the charged amount is immutable once issued; MP preferences remain payable at the snapshot price.

PATCH /api/suscriptions/<id>/ {plan_suscription}: PENDING_PAYMENT branch (lines 74-83) rewrites plan_suscription directly to the expensive plan; ACTIVE branch (line 90) -> RequestPlanChangeQuery sets pending_plan_suscription=expensive + pending_charge=prorated.

Lines 132-135: upgrade sets pending_plan_suscription=target_plan and pending_charge=_upgrade_charge(...) (prorated); downgrade sets pending_plan only. Live-preapproval realignment is best-effort — exceptions swallowed at lines 136-141, so MP can keep debiting the old amount.

MP notification for the stale cheap payment arrives at POST /api/payments/webhook/ (or via POST /api/payments/sync/ viewset.py:432 or POST /api/payments/ create) -> PaymentWebhookQuery -> CreatePaymentQuery with the attacker-owned suscription.

`if amount not in accepted_amounts` — the cheap amount passes because accepted_amounts (lines 115-123) contains EVERY non-trial plan price; the pending/expensive entitlement is never bound to the paid amount.

Lines 287-313: pending_plan applied to plan_suscription unconditionally on APPROVED; prorated gate (281-286) requires paid_amount == pending_charge exactly, so any other accepted amount -> prorated=False -> end_date = now+30d, status=ACTIVE, period_payment_id=payment. Expensive plan granted at cheap-tier price.

evidence.description: accepted_amounts = {plan_price (pending_plan or plan), current plan price, *(ALL SuscriptionPlan.objects.filter(is_trial=False).values_list('price')), pending_charge} — union of every paid plan price, membership-only check at line 124.
prorated = pending_plan AND pending_charge AND paid_amount == pending_charge — any other accepted amount takes the full-renewal branch (296-313): start=now, end=now+30d, status=ACTIVE.
PENDING_PAYMENT branch rewrites plan_suscription directly (lines 79-82) — no pending_plan indirection, so a stale cheap preference pays for whatever plan is currently set.
UpdatePreapprovalPlanQuery realignment is best-effort inside try/except — a failed MP update leaves the preapproval debiting the old cheap amount, recurring the mismatch monthly.

test_debit_at_previous_plan_price_is_registered codifies symmetric acceptance: pending_plan=cheap(500), payment at current plan price(1000) -> APPROVED + pending_plan applied + pending cleared — deliberate design, the exploit primitive in mirror image.

IssueInvoiceQuery reads suscription.plan_suscription.name AFTER ApplyPendingPlanQuery (called at payments/services.py:146->149) -> plan_name=expensive plan while total=payment.amount=cheap (line 85): fiscally inconsistent receipt, CAE requested on the cheap total.

Sibling comparison: seller-side MP webhook requires amount == order.total exactly; mismatch -> amount_mismatch flag + OrderEvent for manual review (fail-closed). The platform subscription path accepts any plan price (fail-open).
Seeded plans differ in price — 25000/30000/40000/60000 ARS — giving a real spread for the cheapest-to-most-expensive arbitrage.

conditions.description: Attacker holds a platform account (store-owner principal) with billing fields complete — BillingMissingFieldsQuery (payments/views/viewset.py:275-280) only requires fiscal profile data, trivially supplied.
At least two non-trial SuscriptionPlans with different prices — the seeded default set (25000/30000/40000/60000 ARS) satisfies this out of the box.

A payable stale-amount MP artifact bound to external_reference=<own suscription.id>: a Checkout Pro preference issued before the plan change keeps its creation-time unit_price (standard MP behavior the codebase explicitly relies on, services.py:107-112), or a preapproval debit generated before realignment.
The attacker must complete the cheap-tier MP payment with real funds at the lower plan price — no provider misbehavior, race, or admin action is required; the sequence is fully deterministic.

execution.attacker_perspective: Registered DAVENT platform user with a complete billing profile and >=2 priced plans available (seeded default).
payloads: Variant A (pending_payment): 1) POST /api/payments/checkout/ {"plan_suscription": <cheap_pk>} -> creates pending_payment Suscription + MP preference P1 (unit_price=cheap.price, external_reference=<sub_id>) 2) PATCH /api/suscriptions/<sub_id>/ {"plan_suscription": <expensive_pk>} -> plan_suscription=expensive (PENDING_PAYMENT branch) 3) Pay P1 in MP Checkout ($cheap) -> payment approved, external_reference=<sub_id>, transaction_amount=cheap 4) POST /api/payments/sync/ {"payment_id": <mp_payment_id>} (or await webhook) -> Payment APPROVED, Suscription ACTIVE plan=expensive end_date=+30d

Variant B (active upgrade): 1) On an ACTIVE cheap-plan subscription with auto_renew off: POST /api/payments/checkout/ {} -> preference P2 at cheap full price 2) PATCH /api/suscriptions/<sub_id>/ {"plan_suscription": <expensive_pk>} -> pending_plan=expensive, pending_charge=prorated 3) Pay stale P2 ($cheap) -> Payment APPROVED; paid_amount != pending_charge -> prorated=False -> pending expensive plan applied AND end_date=now+30d

Recurring: repeat the downgrade-pending + stale-cheap-preference + upgrade-pending cycle each period, or keep a live preapproval whose UpdatePreapprovalPlanQuery realignment failed (best-effort, exceptions swallowed) so monthly debits keep arriving at the old cheap amount and each renews the expensive plan +30d.
instructions: Ensure billing fields are complete (GET subscription -> billing_required fields if any).

Create the cheap-priced MP artifact first: POST /api/payments/checkout/ while the subscription targets the cheap plan (variant A: fresh pending_payment sub; variant B: active cheap-plan sub). Do NOT pay it yet.

Change the granted/target plan to the expensive one via PATCH /api/suscriptions/<id>/ {"plan_suscription": <expensive_pk>} (or POST /api/payments/checkout/ {"suscription": <id>, "plan_suscription": <expensive_pk>}, which also issues a new expensive preference while leaving the cheap one payable).
Pay the earlier cheap preference in the MP Checkout UI — it charges the snapshot cheap price with external_reference=<sub_id>.
Trigger registration: await the MP webhook, or POST /api/payments/sync/ {"payment_id": <id>}, or POST /api/payments/ {"suscription": <id>, "payment_id": <id>}.

Observe: Payment row amount=cheap_price status=approved; Suscription.plan_suscription=expensive, status='Suscripcion activa', end_date=now+30d; Invoice total=cheap_price plan_name=expensive; grants_access()=True -> full expensive-tier benefits for 30 days at cheap-tier price.
execution.observed_result: Source-derived (read-only audit, MP not contacted): CreatePaymentQuery accepts amount=cheap because it is in accepted_amounts (all non-trial plan prices); Payment created APPROVED; ApplyPendingPlanQuery applies pending_plan (or the already-rewritten plan_suscription for pending_payment) and sets end_date=now+30d with status=ACTIVE; IssueInvoiceQuery emits invoice with plan_name=expensive plan and total=cheap amount. grants_access() returns True -> expensive-tier benefits at cheap-tier price, repeatable monthly.

remediation.strategy: Bind the accepted amount to the granted entitlement instead of unioning all plan prices. Compute expected = pending_charge if set else (pending_plan or plan_suscription).price for pending_payment contexts; accept only that amount for auto-apply. For genuinely stale MP artifacts (amount equals a DIFFERENT plan's price), resolve amount->plan and grant THAT plan — never the pending/pricier one — or reject and route to audit_orphan_payments/manual reconciliation like the storepayments sibling (exact amount match + amount_mismatch review). Also make UpdatePreapprovalPlanQuery realignment failure handling consistent so a stale-amount debit cannot recur monthly unnoticed (surface the failure instead of only logging).

amount              =   Decimal(str(mp_payment.get('transaction_amount', '0')))
    pending_plan        =   suscription.pending_plan_suscription
    plan_price          =   (pending_plan or suscription.plan_suscription).price
    expected_amount     =   suscription.pending_charge if suscription.pending_charge is not None else plan_price
    #El monto solo puede acreditar el cargo/plan que se está aplicando.
    #Un monto de OTRO plan es un artefacto viejo de MP: se mapea monto->plan
    #y se otorga ESE plan (nunca uno más caro que el cobrado), o se rechaza
    #para reconciliación manual — copiar la regla de storepayments
    #(amount == expected exacto, mismatch -> revisión).
    accepted_amounts    =   {Decimal(str(expected_amount))}
    stale_plan          =   None
    if amount not in accepted_amounts:
        stale_plan  =   SuscriptionPlan.objects.filter(is_trial = False, price = amount).first()
        if stale_plan is None:
            raise serializers.ValidationError({
                'payment_id':   f'El monto del pago (${amount}) no coincide con el importe esperado (${expected_amount})'
            })

likelihood.reason: Requires deliberate multi-step API orchestration plus a real (lower-tier) MP payment and >=2 priced plans — all within any registered user's capability, fully deterministic, needing no provider misbehavior or race. The stale-preference artifact is standard MP Checkout Pro behavior the codebase already documents. Repeatable monthly via the preference cycle or a failed best-effort preapproval realignment.

impact.reason: Direct recurring revenue loss bounded by the plan price spread per billing period (e.g. 25000 vs 60000 ARS -> top tier at entry-tier price, repeatable). Also produces fiscally inconsistent invoices (expensive plan_name, cheap total, CAE requested) — a compliance/reconciliation problem. Does not grant admin access or cross-tenant data; impact is confined to plan-tier benefits and billing integrity.

confidence.reason: Every in-repo link verified in current source: the union check (services.py:115-124), both plan-change paths (serializers.py:74-90, suscriptions/services.py:102-142), the webhook/sync/POST entry points, the prorated-vs-full-renewal gate (services.py:281-313), the symmetric-acceptance test (tests.py:1249-1265), and the invoice inconsistency (invoices/services.py:72,85). The only external fact — an MP Checkout Pro preference/preapproval debit retains its creation-time amount and delivers it with external_reference=sub_id — is definitional provider behavior explicitly relied upon in code comments (services.py:107-112) and matching the sibling integration's assumptions.
